slides.label: Exercises For Act V
slides.notes: Open the review as a laboratory, not as a list of answers. The chapter gathers the Act V skills and asks students to recognize the object, choose an inspectable model, measure an invariant, and perturb the setup. The dashboard figure gives the rhythm: construct, measure, compare, and rerun.

slides.label: The Forms Ladder
slides.notes: Use this slide to rebuild the hierarchy. A 1-form tests a directed segment, a 2-form tests an oriented surface element, and a 3-form tests an oriented volume element. The exterior derivative moves up the ladder, while integration asks which geometric input is appropriate for the degree of the form.

slides.label: 1-Forms Test Directional Input
slides.notes: Return to the most concrete exercise family. A covector is not a small arrow; it is a linear test on an arrow. The delta-like picture is useful because it makes concentration visible: the same input vector receives its scalar reading from how it crosses the measurement slices.

slides.label: Tensor Contraction Removes A Matched Slot
slides.notes: Frame contraction as controlled bookkeeping. A tensor can carry several slots, but a contraction pairs one upper-lower or matching input-output slot and sums over the repeated index. The heatmap is a ledger: information is not thrown away randomly, it is traced through a specified match.

slides.label: Wedge Products Need Available Dimensions
slides.notes: The wedge product slide is a dimension test. Alternation makes repeated directions vanish, so a proposed product survives only when enough independent directions are available. This is why the same formal expression can be active in one ambient dimension and forced to zero in another.

slides.label: Exterior Derivative Converts Local Readings
slides.notes: Make the exterior derivative feel like a boundary detector. It turns a function into a 1-form, a 1-form into a circulation 2-form, and a flux 2-form into a density 3-form. The compact identities d squared equals zero, curl grad equals zero, and div curl equals zero are the same structural statement.

slides.label: Integration Theorems Compare Boundary And Interior
slides.notes: This is the Stokes checkpoint. Every version compares an integral over a boundary with an integral over the region that boundary encloses. Students should say what the boundary is, which form is being integrated there, and how the exterior derivative becomes the interior measurement.

slides.label: Closed Is Local; Exact May Be Global
slides.notes: Separate the two tests. Closed means the exterior derivative has vanished locally. Exact means the form came from a lower-degree potential globally. The cohomology figure reminds students that topology can block the global potential even when every small patch looks harmless.

slides.label: Moving Frames Turn Forms Into Curvature Probes
slides.notes: Close the technical arc with Cartan's equations. A moving coframe records local measurement axes, connection forms record how the frame turns, and curvature forms record the defect that remains after differentiating the connection. The helix picture makes a frame field visible along a path.

slides.label: Act V Synthesis Checkpoint
slides.notes: End with diagnostic questions rather than new material. Ask students to identify the input geometry, the degree of the form, the invariant being checked, and the theorem that relates two measurements. That habit is the transferable skill from the exercise chapter into later geometry.
